sections.heading: Objective 1: Autonomous Customer Service Agent
bullets: Building on the pre-project supervised drafting assistant (0% autonomy), we extended the continuous draft-vs-final judging system that measures autonomous readiness, and June scored 67.7% of AI drafts sent with no or cosmetic edits (294 drafts judged), up from the 64.7% pre-project baseline (785 drafts) and tracking toward the 80% Contribution Agreement target.

We launched a shadow-mode auto-send experiment on June 11 with a deliberately conservative gate (one low-risk reply category, a hardcoded never-list for anything touching money or orders), which recorded 3 would-have-sent drafts and probes whether autonomous sending can hold quality before real autonomy is enabled.

We built out the exchange, refund, and hold workflows (deterministic price-difference calculation, SKU refund allocation across duplicate line items, and automatic order freezing on changes) so the agent can execute multi-step actions rather than only drafting text.

Founder active customer-service handling time measured 12.8 hours in June (about 3.0 hours/week), down from a roughly 10 hours/week pre-project level, though the two are measured differently and so are only directional.

sections.heading: Objective 1: Platform Reliability Under Load
bullets: We diagnosed that provider overload errors (HTTP 529) and latency were caused by enforced structured-output (JSON schema) mode on large prompts, an open question about whether schema-enforced output can be production-reliable.

We built and live-validated a load-shed circuit breaker that gracefully degrades to a legacy output mode when recent overload errors are detected, plus a degraded-output guard that routes malformed model output to a human.
We added an intake dead-letter replay and automatic drift-noise resolution so failed ticket intake recovers rather than silently dropping.

sections.heading: Objective 2: Partner Channel Discovery and Outreach
bullets: Extending early prospect-scraping and lead-scoring prototypes, we completed backlog research yielding 41 qualified partners and 144 community organizations, and added a Haiku-based pre-filter triage of the unprocessed prospect backlog.

We built a first-version outreach engine (message schemas, cadence evaluators, reply correlation, a six-tier queue, and a two-advisor draft-and-send flow) that remains hard-gated off by default pending validation.
We added an outreach queue panel to the dashboard and seeded relationship state from existing status and order history, laying groundwork toward the 85% qualification-precision target.

sections.heading: Objective 3: Growth Intelligence Groundwork
bullets: We began a Traffic and Conversion Intelligence initiative using a GA4-to-BigQuery export, an early step toward the unified ingestion pipeline the project targets.

We added an email reporting system with audience and session feeds and a weekly marketing content and SEO loop, extending the standalone reporting scripts that existed at project start toward automated synthesis.
